Rashi on Makkot 2b:1:1.hebrew: ומה הסוקל אינו נסקל - עדים שלא הוזמו עד שנהרג הנדון ואח"כ הוזמו, אין נהרגין, כדאמרינן בפרקין (דף ה:): הרגו אין נהרגין, דכתיב: "כאשר זמם", ולא כאשר עשה:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:1:1.english: And if one who stones is not stoned - Witnesses who were not rendered conspiring witnesses until the condemned man was executed, and afterward were rendered conspiring witnesses, are not executed, as we say in our chapter (5b): If they killed, they are not executed, for it is written: "as he conspired" — and not as he did.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:1:2.english: One who came to stone and did not stone - For he was rendered a conspiring witness before the accused was executed.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:3:1.hebrew: הוא שעשה מעשה במזיד אינו גולה - ההורג, שעשה מעשה, אם במזיד עשאו אינו גולה, ואפילו בזמן שאינו נהרג, כגון במזיד בלא התראה:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:3:1.english: He, who performed an action, intentionally is not exiled - The killer, who performed an action — if he did it intentionally, he is not exiled, even at a time when he is not executed, such as when he killed intentionally without forewarning.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:3:2.hebrew: הם שלא עשו מעשה - אלא דיבור בעלמא, ובמזיד העידו, אינו דין שלא יגלו על המזיד:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:3:2.english: They, who did not perform an action - Rather, mere speech, and they testified intentionally — is it not logical that they should not be exiled for an intentional [act]?

Rashi on Makkot 2b:4:1.hebrew: ומקשינן לרבי יוחנן והיא הנותנת - המדה הזאת שהבאת לפטרן, היא הנותנת להם חובת גלות. הוא, לפי שעושה מעשה, אם במזיד עשאו אינו גולה, דלא תהוי ליה כפרה:
Rashi on Makkot 2b:4:1.english: And we challenge Rabbi Yochanan: And that [very distinction] provides [the opposite] - This reasoning that you brought to exempt them is [the very thing] that gives them an obligation of exile. He [the murderer], since he performs an action, if he did it intentionally he is not exiled, so that he will not have atonement.

Rashi on Makkot 2b:4:2.hebrew: הם שלא עשו מעשה יגלו - על זדונן, כי היכי כו':
Rashi on Makkot 2b:4:2.english: They, who did not perform an action, let them be exiled - for their intentional false testimony, so that, etc.

Tosafot on Makkot 2b:1:1.hebrew: ומה הסוקל אינו נסקל - פי' הקונטרס: כשהרגו אין נהרגין, דין הוא דבאו להרוג ולא הרגו דאין נהרגין. וקשה טובא: חדא, דה"ל למימר, כדאמרינן לקמן (מכות דף ה:): "הרגו אין נהרגין"! ועוד, מאי פריך? שאני הכא, דגלי קרא בהדיא דהבא לסקול ולא סקל דנסקל, בההוא קרא גופיה דחזינן דהסוקל אינו נסקל, כדכתיב: "כאשר זמם" — ולא כאשר עשה; אבל לעולם אימא לך דאית לך שפיר ק"ו דלעיל דלענין חילול, דהא לא גלי קרא בשום מקום דשייך בדבר הזה שיתחלל הזמה! ועוד קשה, דהוה ליה לתרץ דהתם ודאי לא עבדינן ק"ו, משום דא"כ בטלת תורת עדים זוממין לגמרי, ולא משכחת לה "כאשר זמם"; אבל לעיל, דלא בטלת תורת עדים זוממין, שייך שפיר למיעבד ק"ו! לכך פירש ר"ת דה"ק: "ומה הסוקל אינו נסקל" — פירוש: אדם שסוקל חבירו באבנים ומת, דנדון בסייף ולא בסקילה; "הבא ליסקל ולא נסקל" — עדים שמעידין איש פלוני שמחויב סקילה ולא נסקל על ידם, "אינו דין שלא יסקלנו"? והשתא לא בטלת לגמרי, דאיכא לאוקומי קרא ד"ועשיתם כאשר זמם" כשהן מעידין שמחויב שאר מיתות ב"ד שאינו בסקילה. ואפ"ה לא עבדינן האי ק"ו, דהכי קאמר לו לעיל דלא עבדינן ק"ו בכהאי גוונא:
Tosafot on Makkot 2b:1:1.english: "And if one who stones is not stoned" - The commentary of Rashi explained: When they have had the defendant executed they are not executed, is it not logical that when they came to have him executed and did not have him executed, they are not executed? And this is very difficult: First, it should have said the wording, as we say below (Makkot 5b): "If they had him executed, they are not executed"! Furthermore, what is the difficulty the Gemara raises? Here it is different, for the verse explicitly reveals that one who comes to stone and did not stone is himself stoned — in that very verse from which we see that one who stones is not stoned, as it is written: "as he conspired" — and not as he did; whereas I could still say to you that you may well make the kal vachomer above regarding profanation of priesthood, for the verse never revealed anywhere that it applies to this matter that he should become profaned through hazamah! Furthermore, it is difficult that the Gemara should have answered that there we certainly do not make the kal vachomer, because if so, you would abolish the law of conspiring witnesses entirely, and you would never find a case of "as he conspired"; whereas above, where you do not abolish the law of conspiring witnesses, it is well applicable to make the kal vachomer! Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explained that this is what it means: "And if one who stones is not stoned" — meaning: a person who stones his fellow to death with stones, who is judged as a murderer by the sword and not by stoning; "one who comes to have another stoned and he was not stoned" — meaning witnesses who testify that so-and-so is liable to stoning, and he was not stoned through them — "is it not logical that we should not stone him?" And now you do not abolish the law of conspiring witnesses entirely, for one can establish the verse of "and you shall do to him as he conspired" where they testify that he is liable to other court-imposed death penalties that are not by stoning. And even so we do not make this kal vachomer, and thus it says to him that above too we do not make a kal vachomer in such a manner.
